attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, published under his name.

semantics.note: The unhedged 'will' makes this a firm forecast. Reading 'this situation' as Huang's reinstatement and 'them' as AI industry leaders fits the context. The revision restored every element he listed. 'Than you'd ever imagine' is hyperbole.

contract.note: The plain reading (more risk-taking, more cash burn and ignored warnings, then severe business distress, caused by the reinstatement) is ordinary and fair. The contract rightly says there is no deadline, and that the comparison with what a reader would imagine cannot be measured.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 23 Nov 2026 filing confirms the reinstatement and the ongoing investigation. It sets the starting point only and says nothing about later behaviour or distress.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline, assessed on the day it was published. The packet holds no later record of more risk-taking, ignored warnings or business failures caused by the reinstatement, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Nothing having happened yet is not failure under an open horizon. The outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: In context, 'they' means the AI startups that buy from OpenAI and Anthropic. The draft dropped 'all' (quantifier null), but the generic plural plus 'basically' keeps roughly the same broad generalisation, and the contract puts 'They're all' back. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'all basically' as a broad generalisation that needs representative evidence is fair and ordinary. Where a 'wrapper' ends and post-training or independent model development begins is not defined by the speaker, so that interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: Harvey's current documentation says it relies on several outside model providers and routes requests among them. This weakly supports the wrapper description for one firm. The same page also mentions in-house fine-tuning, and one firm cannot show prevalence.

Harvey Tenet: a post-trained open-weight model, released as a research preview in Aug 2026. It complicates a thin-wrapper reading but is a single example, and its production use on the target date is not shown.
WRITER's X6 was post-trained on an open-weight base. It shows dependence on an outside base plus real model work, which cuts both ways. It is a single example.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires representative evidence across the startup population. The packet has only two company examples. They show dependence on outside models together with in-house post-training, which neither clearly proves nor clearly defeats 'basically wrappers'. There is no representative study, so the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully keeps 'any meaningful answer', 'beat-and-raise machine' and the scrutiny clause. But 'his affair has created' scrutiny is a causal claim. The contract's causal_assessment axis fits better than the drafter's 'observation'.

contract.note: The contract defines 'meaningful answer' as a concrete growth explanation and requires growth scrutiny caused by the affair. Both are reasonable readings, but the speaker set no thresholds and named no measure of scrutiny, so the interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: The full reinstatement release covers leadership, confidence and compliance but gives no explanation of demand or financing. This supports the first part only, and only for this announcement.

AFP, 24 Nov 2026: investor doubts continue and investigations include a reported SEC probe of NVIDIA's accounting. This partly supports intense scrutiny after the return, but it does not show the affair caused scrutiny of growth.

U.S. Bank, 13 Nov 2026, before the reinstatement: says the leadership change increases scrutiny of NVIDIA's customer financing, and that demand persists. It is useful as a baseline but outside the target period.

reviews.rationale: The first part is narrowly supported: the reinstatement release gives no growth explanation. The support condition, though, also needs comparative evidence that the affair caused renewed and intense scrutiny of NVIDIA's growth. The packet shows investigations and investor doubts but no before-and-after comparison and no causal link to the affair. Nothing contradicts the claim. The outcome is unresolved.
